findings.kind: candidate for a frozen allocation regression
findings.finding: bounded_rational_value tests Ratio numerator/denominator widths with canonicalizing accessors before meter.read. The retained algebraic preflight repair does not alter this separate recognizer.
findings.next_measurement: Use fresh lazy ratios with canonical values on both sides of the existing 4096-bit recognition boundary. Measure the named helper at insufficient work, preserve generous/unlimited answers, then trace domain-validation callers separately.

findings.kind: static call path requiring dynamic coverage
path: two-atan argument difference or acos endpoint difference
findings.finding: The metered inverse-trig sign implementation constructs argument differences with general constructors. add invokes unlimited internal_structural_eq and rational_offset_parts; exact_rational clones integer payloads. This establishes a source-level constructor path, not that a particular resource failure is reachable with a fixed public allowance.
findings.next_measurement: Freeze valid public-query fixtures whose argument equality rejects cheaply, including different integer bit lengths, then measure wide argument negation/addition and retry proof retention. Preserve all constructor exactness and existing proof paths.

findings.finding: PiLaurentPolynomial::clone_with_work charges one visit and allocates its term vector before each RadicalCoefficient clone performs coefficient preflight. The vector is bounded by eight polynomial terms; no unbounded allocation or public resource regression is established.
findings.next_measurement: Measure allowances just after the visit and before the first unavailable coefficient copy, alongside successful-copy and no-allowance behavior. Keep the eight-term limit and recognition semantics.

findings.kind: existing bounds and distinct remaining work
findings.finding: Laurent recognition already caps aggregate node visits at 512, polynomial terms at eight and radical terms at eight, with charged atom comparisons. The reviewed inverse-trig recognizers use a depth bound and query-local shared-node memoization; their unshared terms still need separate growth measurements. AlgebraicSeparation has its existing 256-node/16-generator/4096-combination guards. These are not native exact-operation time or memory bounds.

Several rational domain cases compare canonical numerator/denominator components after a node debit. A previously published finite-real certificate can bypass these branches. Node construction retains inverse-trig/linear-demand hints, not a finite-real certificate; the inspected finite-real stores occur in successful domain validation. Remaining lazy-reduction and wide-scan exposure needs branch-specific measurement.
